metadata.note: Modern-day SEPTA network, as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://www3.septa.org/developer/gtfs_public.zip (google_rail.zip). Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/amtrak.geojson. Each route is a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added by estimating headway_min at researched ownership/frequency-milestone boundaries (predecessor-railroad origin dates, PRR/Reading Company corporate history, 1915-1935 electrification programs, the 1976 Conrail and 1983 SEPTA takeovers, the 1984 Center City Commuter Connection tunnel that unified the former PRR and Reading networks, etc., sourced from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites); unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, these older headway numbers are not derived from real historical timetables and should be read as illustrative estimates, not precise data.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
